newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf rises, Total firm but lags.
newsitem.headline: Elf rises, Total firm but lags.

text.p: Elf and Total both gained on Friday in a rising market, but Elf outstripped the latter.
One French broker said there was some arbitrage between the oil majors, with Elf benefiting from a premium of around 40 francs over Total, the widest spread seen for some time.

Oils have risen with the firming in world crude prices but Elf was further helped by today's sale of a 10 percent stake in Geophysique and last week's sale of a nine percent stake by the French government.
Elf was up 1.73 percent at 458 francs, while Total was up 0.89 percent at 417.5.
Some operators were buying Elf and selling Total, which pushed out the share price spread between the two stocks, the broker said.
There appeared to be covering of short positions on Elf, after the state's sale of most of its stake in the oil company, he added.
Today's sale of Compagnie Generale de Geophysique shares covered some 400,000 shares at 365 francs per share, with brokerage Du Bouzet handling the placement, market sources said.
